text:
elyse: Quick bring-up for seabird-lite-int6 on wiki_code_holdout_7k. Ran recall@10/100, clustering, and a short-query stress slice. Posting headline numbers and next steps.

kai: TL;DR numbers please

elyse: Baseline (seabird-v2) recall@10 = 0.849. seabird-lite-int6 recall@10 = 0.815 (delta -0.034). recall@100 delta smaller (~-0.011). Paired bootstrap p=0.0009 (1000 resamples).

ben: Oof. Any centroid / norm shifts?

elyse: Mean embedding norm dropped about 4.9% vs baseline. Mean intra-cluster cosine 0.69 -> 0.63. Silhouette (k=120) 0.33 -> 0.25. NN churn (top5) ~15%.

kai: Which query slices break most?

elyse: Symbol-rich queries (code/math) and very short queries (<5 tokens). Example failing query (id 990112): "vector.emplace_back(x)" 1 of top-5 NN changed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for seabird-lite-int6 on 4 nodes at 01:00UTC. Canary policy: auto-revert if recall@10 drop > 2.0% on production trace.

ben: Did you try per-channel quant or bias-correcting output norms? Also try an asymmetric zero-point profile and KV-cache friendly quant profile.

elyse: Per-channel + asymmetric queued. Quick tried hack: multiply vectors by 1.05 (post-quant L2 scaling) -> recall@10 0.815 -> 0.828. Partial recovery but still ~-0.021 vs baseline.

kai: Good to know. Please run a paired bootstrap diff for the scaled vectors too (get p-value).

elyse: Paired bootstrap for scaled run p=0.0012 (still significant).

ben: If per-channel + scaling doesn't close enough, run a 6->5-bit ablation and a hybrid routing test where short queries (<5 tokens) stay on seabird-v2. That often keeps UX safe while letting us ship cost-savings.

elyse: Kicked off these ablations. Repro command:```bash
./eval_holdout.sh --model seabird-lite-int6 --holdout wiki_code_holdout_7k \
  --k 10,100 --resamples 1000 --slices short_queries,code_symbols --save-fail-ids 500
```

viz-bot: viz-bot: UMAP + per-topic neighbor-diff plots uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/6487654321/umap_diff.zip

ben: Make sure artifacts include tokenized signatures (no raw query text) and only sample IDs for privacy. Also include top-200 failed sample IDs for manual QA.

elyse: Will log sample ids + token signatures only. Also adding UMAP color-by-topic and delta-NN heatmaps.

kai: Keep latency profiling in the sweep outputs so we can see cost impact of per-channel/asymmetric vs baseline. If per-channel + scaling recovers >75% of quality gap and latency hit <3% we can consider a controlled canary.

elyse: Agreed. If the canary sees >2% degradation on production traffic we auto-revert (ops-bot already configured). Meanwhile I'll add a short-query routing flag for the canary window: queries <5 tokens -> route to seabird-v2.

ben: Also try tiny isotropic jitter during calibration before quant to reduce quantization cliff for symbol tokens; helped on past models.

elyse: Queued jitter-calibrate run and hybrid 5-bit ablation. Posting final sweep numbers and sample ids in ~1.5 hours. :thumbsup:
